turns.t: Good morning, doctor. Thank you for seeing me. I was told at the kidney clinic that I'm anaemic, and I should come and discuss it.
Good morning, Mrs Fletcher. Yes, I've seen the letter. How have you been feeling lately? ~
Tired, I must say. More than usual. I used to garden every day, and now I sit down after twenty minutes.
And what about your breathing?
A bit short of breath on the hills, and the stairs. Not terrible.
Have you had any chest pain, or dizzy spells, or palpitations? ~
No, none of that, thank goodness. ~
How long has the tiredness been going on? ~
Since the new year. Gradually creeping up.
You have chronic kidney disease, I see, stage three.
Yes, they told me eighteen months ago. It's stable, they say.
That's right. Let me check your pulse and blood pressure. ~
Of course. ~
Pulse 80, blood pressure 132 over 76, oxygen 97 percent.
Are those good? ~
They're fine. I'll also look at your eyelids and your nails, which can show anaemia. ~
Do I look pale? ~
A little. ~
Oh dear. ~
Your blood test last month showed your haemoglobin was low, at 98. Normal for a woman is above 120. ~
That's quite a lot lower. ~
It is, and kidneys make a hormone that tells your bone marrow to make red blood cells, so when the kidneys are weaker, you can become anaemic. ~
So it's the kidneys? ~
I think that's the most likely cause, I'd say anaemia of chronic kidney disease.
Can it be treated? ~
Yes. First, I'd like to arrange more blood tests, to check your iron, vitamin B12 and folate levels, because other causes need ruling out.
Will it need injections? ~
Possibly, if your iron is normal and the anaemia is due to the kidneys. There are injections that help the bone marrow. ~
I'm not keen on injections. ~
They're small, and you can learn to do them yourself. We'll decide after the tests. ~
Right. Anything I can do? ~
Eat iron-rich foods, like red meat, spinach, and beans, and don't take iron tablets until we've checked.
I take a multivitamin. ~
That's fine. ~
And rest? ~
Pace yourself, build up your gardening slowly. I'd like to see you again in two weeks with the results.
Two weeks. Thank you, doctor. ~
